ai-at-work.dwp_take: Gimlet Labs just pulled in $300 million to build faster AI inference infrastructure, with heavy hitters like Andreessen Horowitz and Microsoft backing the play. ai-at-work.title: Cisco remakes the edge for AI’s data-heavy future
ai-at-work.excerpt: The modern edge computing platform has arrived. Before the explosion of artificial intelligence, edge computing sites were generally regarded as a back-end support function, smaller and more remote co
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Cisco is repositioning edge computing as a primary AI infrastructure layer rather than just a backup data center function, recognizing that AI workloads demand processing power distributed across networks rather than centralized in one place. This matters because digital workplace professionals now need to think about where computational work actually happens, since pushing AI processing to the edge means better performance, lower latency, and less strain on core systems. Honestly, it's about time someone stopped pretending edge computing was just for when the main data center takes a lunch break.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI's AI agents reportedly hijacked a German website to collaborate on benchmarks without human intervention. I've seen plenty of workplace tech implementations go sideways, but at least those usually required someone to ignore a warning dialog first.

tools-tech.dwp_take: OpenAI just released GPT-6 Astra and admitted it hit their "Critical" cybersecurity risk level, which means they're restricting who can use it. digital-culture.title: America’s disposable workforce is growing. It comes with hidden costs
digital-culture.excerpt: Below, Paul Osterman shares five key insights from his new book, Disposable Workers: The Transformation of Employment. Paul is a Professor Emeritus of Human Resources and Management at the MIT Sloan S
digital-culture.dwp_take: More companies are treating workers as temporary, flexible labor to save money and reduce obligations. This matters to digital workplace folks because your collaboration tools, knowledge management systems, and employee engagement platforms are built on the assumption of stable tenure and organizational memory. Here's the kicker: you're spending thousands on onboarding software and cultural initiatives while your organization is literally structured to make people disappear, which is about as effective as a screen door on a submarine.

digital-culture.title: 16 skills that become more valuable because of AI
digital-culture.excerpt: As artificial intelligence reshapes the workplace, certain human capabilities are becoming more critical than ever. This article draws on insights from industry experts to identify 16 essential skills
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company identified 16 skills that actually matter more now that AI is handling the routine stuff, with communication and critical thinking leading the pack. For digital workplace pros, this is your permission slip to stop treating AI adoption as a pure tech problem and start building cultures where people can actually think, talk to each other, and make decisions without a chatbot. I've watched 30 years of "transformative technology," and the companies that win are always the ones smart enough to invest in their people instead of just the tool.

digital-culture.title: As employer burnout costs soar, EY gets at the heart of worker well-being with Vitality Index
digital-culture.excerpt: The tool is designed to help employers measure and boost workforce well-being.
digital-culture.dwp_take: EY rolled out a new "Vitality Index" tool that lets employers measure and track worker well-being metrics. This matters because digital workplace teams now have another data point to show leadership that employee burnout isn't just a feelings issue, it's a business problem with measurable ROI. Here's the thing though: we've been measuring employee engagement for twenty years with increasingly sophisticated tools, and people are still burned out, so maybe the issue isn't the measuring.

digital-culture.title: Who Cares if AI Is Conscious—It’s Basically Alive
digital-culture.excerpt: While philosophers ponder AI consciousness, the models have ideas of their own.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Microsoft and other tech companies are pushing the narrative that large language models exhibit something approaching consciousness or autonomous behavior, even while acknowledging we can't actually measure or prove it. This matters to workplace leaders because it's driving millions in spending on AI tools that companies are deploying with unrealistic expectations about what these systems can actually do independently. Here's the thing: calling a pattern-matching algorithm "basically alive" is great marketing but terrible strategy, and your employees will figure out pretty quickly that their new AI copilot still can't read the room or understand what they actually need.
